subject: Application - Senior Site Reliability Engineer (Database Focus)
paragraphs: I am applying for the Senior SRE role with the database focus. Your description puts the database estate at the centre of a payments platform, where a slow query becomes a customer-visible incident, and that framing is why I want the role: the work I have done for four years is keeping a small production estate healthy under exactly that constraint, with one person on call and no room for an alert that cries wolf.

PostgreSQL is where my database work is real rather than adjacent. The fleet's mail archive is Postgres with versioned migrations, a restore that is rehearsed rather than assumed, statement timeouts and disk-pressure alerting wired into the same sentinel that records job status, generation age and pressure stall every fifteen minutes. I read plans before adding indexes, have chased idle-in-transaction sessions and autovacuum lag on my own hardware, and treat a backfill as a change with a rollback plan rather than a query to run and hope about.

The surrounding reliability work is the same shape as your team's: infrastructure declared in code with pinned inputs, a change counted only once a gate has read the built artifact back, secrets encrypted per host and authenticated through a certificate authority, and a vulnerability pipeline driven by the CISA KEV catalogue rather than by the loudest advisory. Services are Go and Python. Observability is self-built, a ledger plus gatus paging on any state that is not ok, which is the smaller equivalent of the Grafana and Datadog work in your stack rather than experience with those tools.

The gap I cannot paper over is the specialty bar: five or more years running PostgreSQL fleets with HA, replication and failover, Stolon or Cloud SQL, and major-version upgrades led end to end with minimal downtime. I have run one production Postgres instance and its recovery path, not an estate, and I have never led a major-version migration. Terraform, GKE, Argo CD and Ruby are also absent from my corpus; Nix is my infrastructure language, and GitOps here is a flake and a task interface. I would be joining as someone strong on the reliability and incident side and learning the database depth from your team, which is worth saying before an interview rather than during one.

On location: your Platform Engineering team is in London, Riga and Lisbon and I am in south-west Germany, CET. I am asking whether the role can be held from Germany rather than assuming it, since that is a decision for you and not something I can settle in a letter.
